title: Hobbies & Preferences
subtitle: Talk about free time, unusual hobbies and what you enjoy.

sections.label: Lesson Notes
sections.title: What makes a hobby?
sections.intro: We discussed holidays, familiar and unusual hobbies, and ways to explain preferences.

cards.title: A hobby
cards.text: A hobby is an activity you do in your free time for enjoyment. People may do it regularly, but they do not need to be experts.

cards.title: From familiar to unusual
cards.text: We discussed gardening, photography, puzzles, coin collecting and toy voyaging. Explain what someone does and why the activity appeals to them.

cards.title: Add a reason
cards.text: A preference becomes more interesting when you explain it: ‘I quite like photography because it helps me notice details.’

cards.title: Enjoy + -ing
cards.text: Use enjoy + a noun or an -ing form for an activity: ‘I enjoy doing puzzles.’ Not: ‘I enjoy to do puzzles.’

cards.title: Like + -ing
cards.text: Like + -ing can describe an activity you enjoy: ‘She likes taking pictures.’ Like can also take an infinitive in many contexts: ‘She likes to take pictures.’

cards.title: Other expressions
cards.text: Use -ing after can't stand and don't mind: ‘I can’t stand waiting.’ ‘I don’t mind doing puzzles.’ After crazy about, use a noun or -ing: ‘I’m crazy about birdwatching.’

cards.title: Strength and meaning
cards.text: ‘I quite like’ expresses a moderate positive preference. ‘I’m crazy about’ is much stronger. ‘I don’t mind’ means it is acceptable, not necessarily a favourite.

cards.title: gardening
cards.text: Growing and looking after plants. ‘He enjoys gardening on weekends.’

cards.title: photography
cards.text: The activity of taking photographs. ‘She’s crazy about photography.’

cards.title: coin collecting
cards.text: Keeping coins as a collection; numismatics is the study or collecting of coins. ‘They enjoy collecting old coins.’

cards.title: do a puzzle
cards.text: Put pieces together to make a picture or solve a problem. ‘We do puzzles on rainy days.’

cards.title: birdwatching
cards.text: Watching birds as a hobby. ‘I quite like birdwatching.’

cards.title: toy voyaging
cards.text: Sending a toy on journeys and following its travels. ‘Toy voyaging is an unusual hobby.’

activities.prompt: Complete: I enjoy ___ (take) pictures when I travel.
activities.example: I enjoy taking pictures when I travel.

activities.prompt: Correct the verb form: She enjoys to do puzzles.
Match the meanings: crazy about / don't mind / can't stand — acceptable / dislike very strongly / like very much.
activities.example: Crazy about = like very much; don't mind = acceptable; can't stand = dislike very strongly.

activities.prompt: Describe one familiar hobby and one unusual hobby. Say which you would try and why.
activities.example: I quite like photography because I enjoy noticing details. Toy voyaging sounds unusual, but I would like to learn more.

readings.title: A collection and a journey
readings.text:
Nora enjoys collecting coins. She looks for coins from different countries and reads about their history. She says each coin can tell a small story about a place.

Her friend Sam has a different hobby: toy voyaging. Sam sends a small toy to friends in other places. They take photographs and share stories about its journey. Nora is curious, but she prefers finding coins. Both friends enjoy talking about their hobbies together.

questions.q: How do Sam's friends help with the hobby?
opt: They take photographs and share stories.

sections.label: Listening
sections.title: Listen to two preferences
sections.intro: Listen to this original dialogue and then explain the two speakers’ preferences. The script remains available below.
sections.audioText: I quite like doing puzzles, but I'm crazy about photography. What about you? I don't mind puzzles, but I can't stand collecting coins. I prefer gardening because I enjoy growing plants.

activities.prompt: Which hobby does the second speaker prefer, and why?
activities.example: The second speaker prefers gardening because they enjoy growing plants.

questions.q: Which expression means ‘I like it very much’?
questions.hint: It is the strongest positive expression.

questions.q: Which activity means looking after plants?
Complete: She can't stand ___ for a bus.
What does ‘I don't mind doing puzzles’ mean?
opt: I only do puzzles for money.
I have never seen a puzzle.
Doing puzzles is acceptable to me.
questions.hint: It is not a strong negative.

questions.q: What does a coin collector collect?
questions.hint: The answer is in the name.

opt: I like gardening because I enjoy plants.
